latin_text: [HARVESTER: from Allen critical translation; source location: Garin edition, Commento 2.22, p. 505]
english_translation: Pico resolves the apparent paradox by declaring that Love is the oldest god, because he existed before the other gods, who, as the Ideas, were to achieve their 'natural' or 'perfected' being only after Love had caused Mind to return to the One and in turn to receive its natural being; in other words, the Ideas were still in Mind imperfectly (secondo il loro essere ideale imperfetto). But he is the youngest and the most beautiful god, because the other gods existed before him, not, as one might have anticipated from Pico's earlier arguments, in their cause, the One, but rather joined to the still unformed substance of Mind in an ideal but imperfect way.
exegesis:
[VERIFIED] Pico resolves Plato's paradox: Love is the *oldest* god because Love existed before the other gods (the Ideas) in their perfected being—Love must arise before the Ideas can achieve their *natural* or *perfected state* (*essere naturale*). Yet Love is the *youngest* because the Ideas existed before Love, though imperfectly (*secondo il loro essere ideale imperfetto*). [INFERRED] This sophisticated resolution distinguishes eternal causation from temporal sequence: in the eternal order of emanation, Love is primordial (it is the principle causing emanation); yet in the logical order of perfection, the Ideas must precede Love in their inchoate form.

The philosophical function is to establish Love as metaphysically prior while avoiding an infinite regress. Love is "first" not chronologically but ontologically—as the principle through which all things achieve their perfected being. Yet the Ideas, though receiving their perfection *through* Love, are not *created by* Love but emanate with it in the single moment of eternal emanation.

[INFERRED] This grounds the mystical theology: the human soul, participating in Love, participates in the very principle through which all creation is perfected. Heptaplus describes this as the perpetual emanation across seven days. Being & Unity explains: Love is the dynamic principle of participation itself.
kabbalistic_elements: The tension between old and young parallels Kabbalistic doctrine of the simultaneous and eternal emanation of Sefiroth.

other_texts: Plotinus on temporal and eternal causation

notes: HARVESTER context: Sophisticated resolution of the Platonic temporal paradox through the distinction between eternal and temporal causation. Source: Allen, p. 6290-6302; Garin edition, Commento 2.22, p. 505. Kabbalistic density: MODERATE (simultaneous emanation of Sefiroth).
